newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-BACHER SLAMS CROWD BEHAVIOUR.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BACHER SLAMS CROWD BEHAVIOUR.

text.p: The United Cricket Board of South Africa managing director, Ali Bacher, has criticised the crowd behaviour at Kingsmead during Wednesday night's match and said everything would be done to prevent future incidents.

"What happened here tonight was a disgrace to both Natal and South African cricket," Bacher said after the day/night final of the triangular series between South Africa and India was washed out by rain.
With South Africa 42 for one in reply to India's 191 for nine, play was halted by steady drizzle and scores of inebriated spectators invaded the field.
The match was also marked by a number of fist fights in the capacity crowd of 21,000 and several explosions caused by fire- crackers which were thrown onto the field.
"This sort of behaviour just cannot be allowed," said Bacher. "It follows other crowd incidents at Benoni and Buffalo Park earlier this season."
"Structures must now be put up at all the test grounds to make it difficult for spectators to invade the field of play.
"Centurion Park are planning a moat between the field and the crowd area and here at Kingsmead they are talking about a picket fence-type of barrier," he said.
